text: Finding friends takes coordination. A survey of fifteen hundred adult festival-goers found forty-four percent used group chats, forty-three percent calls, and forty percent live location.
SafeNight brings that into one place. See your group, their shared locations, and a timeline of everyone's check-ins.
Invite friends, ask someone to come to you, or open driver concerns and venue reports.
Group messages keep everyone updated when someone misses a check-in or asks for help.
Here, the demo agent brings the situation together: who needs help, their last location, and which friend can respond.
The plan suggests walking over, calling a backup, or offering a ride. A friend accepts the next step. Here’s what a check-in call can sound like.
Finding someone takes more than a pin. Connect the paths, find a route, and start moving toward your friend.
The map puts the group in context, then opens a walking route to Maya. Expand it for a closer look, and follow the directions as your position updates.
Switch to the compass view for direction and distance. Walking progress stays visible, with a control to pause it.
Back in messages, the group knows who is on the way. In a private conversation, Maya can share the details that help her friend find her.

SpacetimeDB keeps shared state in sync. Nemotron powers the coordination workflow. ElevenLabs and Photon support voice calls, while OpenStreetMap supplies map and route data. This recording uses a labeled demo scenario.
As the route progresses, the gap gets smaller. The goal is simple: less time searching, and a clearer plan for getting back together.
SafeNight. Go out together. Get home together.
